title: The 8 Best IT Inventory Management Software
summary: Compare the best IT inventory management software options for growing teams, including Rippling and Firstbase, with key features and pricing.
body_markdown:
Every company laptop moves through the same lifecycle. It’s bought and shipped, fixed and replaced as needed, then retrieved after[offboarding](https://www.rippling.com/blog/the-hr-professionals-guide-to-employee-offboarding) and reused until your company decides to upgrade. On a distributed team, each of these steps can land in a different country, with a different carrier, and with nobody entirely sure whose job it is. Devices quickly become everyone’s problem and nobody’s task.


Every step costs your IT team time, especially if your processes are handled manually. In fact, Rippling’s[State of the IT Leader](https://www.rippling.com/resources/itleaderreport) ** survey revealed that over half of IT leaders (51%) spend significant time on onboarding and offboarding alone, and nearly seven in 10 (68.3%) pull the data those processes rely on, in part, by hand. IT inventory management software is designed to save your IT team time on these repetitive admin tasks. Instead of scouring through spreadsheets and Slack threads from months past, you get one record that shows where each device is and what shape it’s in. This guide covers nine platforms, ranging from free open-source tools to services that manage device storage and shipping. It also covers the pricing, features, and customer feedback that set each option apart.


## The 9 best IT inventory management software options for businesses


Here's how the nine IT inventory management software options compare in terms of best fit, standout features, and starting price.


**Best For**


**Features**


**Pricing**


1. Rippling IT


Teams that want inventory tied to HR and device management


End-to-end global logistics, automated retrieval, Device Buyback

2. Snipe-IT


Budget-conscious teams comfortable with self-hosting


Open source, unlimited users and assets, license tracking


Free (self-hosted); hosted from $39.99/month


3. NinjaOne


Teams that want asset inventory inside endpoint management


Unified asset inventory, warranty tracking, license insights


$1.50 to $3.75/device/month

Distributed teams outsourcing global logistics


150+ country visibility, MDM sync, resale credits


Custom quote

Custom quote

Teams managing assets through a service desk


Asset discovery, CMDB, software, and SaaS management


From $19/agent/month

IT teams that want dedicated ITAM with published pricing

## Methodology


To create an objective comparison of the top IT inventory management software, I evaluated each platform on the same five criteria, using vendor documentation and published pricing pages, product walkthroughs where available, and trusted third-party review sites:


1.


**Inventory depth:** How well the tool tracks hardware and software, whether it discovers devices automatically or relies on manual entry, how it assigns assets to employees and locations, and what reporting it offers for audits and budgeting.


2.


**Lifecycle coverage:** Whether the tool supports every stage of a device's life, from procurement and deployment to retrieval at offboarding and sale.


3.


**Integrations:** How the tool connects with HR, identity, MDM, and service desk systems, and whether employee changes update inventory records automatically or require manual work.


4.


**Pricing transparency:** Whether the vendor publishes pricing and how it scales (per user, per device, per agent, or by asset count). I sourced all prices from each vendor's website as of September 2026, and custom quote tools are noted.


5.


**User sentiment:** Ratings, review volume, and recurring themes from G2, Capterra, and TrustRadius, including positive and negative feedback.


**Why Rippling IT ranked first**


Rippling IT scored strongly on inventory depth, lifecycle coverage, and integrations at the same time. It tracks devices from the same employee record that runs HR and payroll, handles end-to-end global logistics across 130 different countries, automates retrieval at offboarding, and issues data-wiping certificates through Device Buyback.


***Rippling editorial policy:*** *Rippling puts our customers (and prospective customers!) first. The Rippling team is committed to providing information supported by product data, insights, and customer feedback to inform our content.*


## 1. Rippling IT


[Rippling IT](https://www.rippling.com/blog/meet-rippling-it) manages inventory from the same employee record that runs HR and payroll, so hiring, role changes, and offboarding automatically trigger device actions. You don’t have to switch HR systems to get that automation, either. Rippling IT also runs as a standalone product that pulls employee data from your existing HRIS or identity provider.


For instance, when someone leaves,[Rippling AI](https://www.rippling.com/platform/ai) sends a padded box with a prepaid label and tracks the return to the nearest available warehouse. There, the device is inspected, wiped, and queued for redeployment.


So, if a remote account executive in Denver leaves and her replacement starts in Austin three weeks later, IT can reassign the same laptop from the employee record instead of buying a new one.


That single-record structure is what IT teams tend to notice first. Alex Yonetani, Head of IT at Jasper, says, “The fact that everything is all together and I don’t have to go in and link different systems between HCM and MDM makes it easy. \[With Rippling,\] we have one place to manage users and devices, as well as our onboarding and offboarding processes, which is great.”


“


The fact that everything is all together and I don’t have to go in and link different systems between HCM and MDM makes it easy. \[With Rippling,\] we have one place to manage users and devices, as well as our onboarding and offboarding processes, which is great.


Alex Yonetani


Head of IT at Jasper


Rippling IT holds a 4.7/5 rating on G2 across 1,100+ reviews. On TrustRadius, a[people operations lead](https://www.trustradius.com/reviews/rippling-2026-04-22-07-16-42) reports a 30–40% drop in onboarding time, and a[technology manager](https://www.trustradius.com/reviews/rippling-2026-07-08-12-40-14) says there's less guessing about who has which device. Both note that setup takes work: building workflows and configuring policies takes time, and the documentation could be clearer.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Less time tracking who has which device


Workflow, policy, and integration setup takes time


30-40% faster onboarding, per one reviewer


Platform documentation could be clearer


### Pricing


Modular pricing based on the modules you choose, starting at $8/employee/month with a free trial available. Device ordering through the Rippling Store is available in the US and Canada.


### Key features


-


**Global logistics:** End-to-end logistics handled across 130+ countries, with every laptop arriving in “Zero-Touch” configuration with security policies and software pre-installed.


-


**Automated retrieval:** Padded boxes, prepaid labels, and return tracking triggered by offboarding.


-


**Device Buyback:** Real-time resale value and data-wiping certificates for retired devices.


Track and manage all IT assets effortlessly


[See Rippling IT](https://www.rippling.com/request-rippling-it-live-tour)


## 2. Snipe-IT


Snipe-IT is free, open-source IT asset tracking software for teams that want full control over their data. Self-hosting costs nothing, and paid hosting plans remove the server work. It tracks hardware, software licenses, and assignments, while procurement and shipping stay with your team.


If you have in-house technical skills and want free, self-hosted asset tracking, Snipe-IT does the job. G2 users rate it 4.6/5 across 26 reviews. On TrustRadius, an[IT director](https://www.trustradius.com/reviews/snipe-it-2026-07-17-17-10-09) uses it for inventory management, offboarding collection, and holding employees accountable for assigned equipment, and says it’s simple for end users to find what’s assigned to them.


There’s a catch, and it's a laborious one. The same reviewer says tweaking it can require scripting and config file changes outside the UI, and that checking items back in from a user means checking in each item individually.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Inventory tracking with user accountability


Some configurations require work outside the UI


End users can easily find their assigned gear


Items must be checked in one at a time


### Pricing


Free to self-host. Basic hosting starts at $39.99/month, Small Business Hosting costs $99.99/month or $399.99/year, and dedicated hosting starts at $249.99/month.


### Key features


-


**Open source:** No license fees or vendor lock-in when self-hosted.


-


**Unlimited users and assets:** Included on every hosted plan.


-


**Hardware and license tracking:** One record for devices and the software assigned to them.


## 3. NinjaOne


NinjaOne is a unified IT operations platform that combines endpoint management, patching, and remote support with built-in IT asset management. Its inventory pulls hardware, software, and lifecycle records into a single view, regardless of whether a device is agent-managed, discovered on the network, or offline. It also tracks warranties and software usage to help teams right-size licenses and plan refreshes.


The platform is rated 4.7/5 on G2. On TrustRadius, an[IT team member at a 501–1,000-person company](https://www.trustradius.com/reviews/ninjaone-2025-02-28-16-55-15) says it made patching and security upkeep across their devices much easier and that they deployed it to their fleet within days, and a[CTO at an IT consultancy](https://www.trustradius.com/reviews/ninjaone-2025-02-25-16-15-27) highlights its update management, remote support options, and documentation features.


Weigh the trade-offs, though: the same CTO notes that its MDM is still new, antivirus integrations are limited, and the cost isn’t low, while the first reviewer would like easier support for application updates.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Simplifies patching across the device fleet


MDM is still new, and AV integrations are limited


Remote support and documentation tools


Pricing isn’t low


### Pricing


Per-device pricing varies by region and products purchased, from as low as $1.50/device/month at 10,000 endpoints to $3.75/device/month at 50 or fewer endpoints. A 14-day free trial is available.


### Key features


-


**Unified asset inventory:** Managed, unmanaged, online, and offline assets in one record.


-


**Warranty and lifecycle tracking:** Lifecycle events and device warranties for budget planning.


-


**License insights:** Software usage data to reclaim and right-size licenses.


## 4. Firstbase


Firstbase pairs asset tracking software with its own global logistics operation. It shows devices across 150+ countries in a single view, keeps pre-stocked inventory in global warehouses, and handles procurement, deployment, storage, retrieval, and disposal. Firstbase reports a 97%+ device retrieval rate and pays resale credits for retired hardware quarterly.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Handles global procurement and recovery


Few official ITSM integrations


If you’re hiring remotely across many countries and want someone else to handle device logistics, Firstbase is built for that. G2 reviewers rate it 4.7/5 across 51 reviews. One G2 reviewer at a remote-first software company says[Firstbase’s global procurement and recovery](https://www.g2.com/products/firstbase-firstbase/reviews/firstbase-review-11280560) saves their small corporate IT team time when packaging and shipping equipment to new hires.


They also say recovering equipment outside the U.S. is now manageable, even without offices or IT staff in most countries where they have employees. If you rely on a service desk platform, check integrations early: the same reviewer would like more official integrations with tools like ITSMs, beyond what Firstbase’s API allows.


### Pricing


Custom quote based on employee count, countries, and the services you need.


### Key features


-


**Global coverage:** One view of devices across 150+ countries.


-


**MDM sync:** Real-time integration with JumpCloud, Jamf, and Intune.


-


**Asset recovery:** Resale credits for retired devices, paid quarterly.


Manage identity, devices, and inventory from a single platform.


[Explore IT](https://www.rippling.com/products/it)


## 5. Asset Panda


Asset Panda is a configurable asset tracking platform that covers IT hardware alongside non-IT equipment so that organizations can track laptops, tools, and facilities assets in one place. It includes barcode tracking, mobile asset auditing, reservation management for shared equipment, and maintenance workflows.


Asset Panda is rated 4.6/5 on Capterra from more than 1,300 reviews and 4.2/5 on G2 from 42 reviews.[One G2 reviewer](https://www.g2.com/products/asset-panda/reviews/asset-panda-review-12045515) finds tracking each laptop’s location, age, and assignment invaluable, since they can quickly sort the data to see which employee has the oldest laptop and plan replacements.


They also praise its reporting and data extraction for managing the asset lifecycle. Budget time for data entry, though: the same reviewer finds entering new assets tedious and slow, and would like device details to fill in automatically from the serial number.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Tracks laptop location, age, and assignment


Manual asset entry is slow


### Pricing


Custom quote based on the plan and features you need, with a free trial available.


### Key features


-


**Barcode tracking:** Scan barcode labels to quickly find assets and update their records.


-


**Mobile auditing:** Take inventory into the field and complete audits from your phone or tablet.


-


**Custom configuration:** Set up fields and workflows to match how you track different types of assets.


## 6. Freshservice


Freshservice is an IT service management platform from Freshworks with IT asset management built into its service desk. The ITAM Growth package covers discovery for Windows, macOS, and Linux devices, hardware asset and lifecycle management, and a CMDB, with both agentless and agent-based discovery. The Pro package adds contracts, purchase orders, software asset management, and SaaS discovery.


If your IT team already runs requests through a service desk, Freshservice keeps assets in the same place as your tickets. It’s rated 4.6/5 on G2 across more than 1,300 reviews and 8.3/10 on TrustRadius. On TrustRadius, a[senior IT service desk analyst](https://www.trustradius.com/reviews/freshservice-2026-08-26-10-57-21) uses it to monitor both tickets and assets and finds it easier to navigate than ServiceNow, and an[IT engineer](https://www.trustradius.com/reviews/freshservice-2026-09-29-14-15-08-995) says it’s great for tracking onboarding, offboarding, and other tasks that span multiple departments.


Discovery is where reviewers get burned. An[IT administrator](https://www.trustradius.com/reviews/freshservice-2026-08-26-10-51-38) calls asset tracking their main gripe, noting that the Freshservice agent doesn’t always record new devices entering their Intune tenant, and that the IT engineer finds auditing agent activity difficult.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Monitors tickets and assets in one place


Agent doesn’t always pick up new Intune devices


Tracks onboarding and offboarding across departments


Auditing agent activity is difficult


### Pricing


Service desk plans start at $19/agent/month, billed annually (Starter), with Growth at $49/agent/month and Pro at $99/agent/month. Growth and higher plans include the ITAM Growth package with 100 asset units, and standalone ITAM plans are quote-based.


### Key features


-


**Asset discovery:** Agentless and agent-based scans for laptops, servers, and network and cloud equipment.


-


**CMDB:** Configuration records that connect assets to incidents and changes.


-


**Software and SaaS management:** License tracking and SaaS discovery on the Pro ITAM package.


## 7. ManageEngine AssetExplorer


ManageEngine AssetExplorer, from Zoho's ManageEngine division, is a dedicated IT asset management tool available in the cloud or on-premises. It discovers hardware and software through agent-based and agentless scans, supports barcode, QR code, and RFID scanners, and tracks software license compliance. A built-in CMDB, plus purchase order and contract management, covers assets from purchase through expiration.


If you want a dedicated IT asset management tool with published pricing and a free tier, put AssetExplorer on your list. It’s rated 4.2/5 on G2 across 13 reviews and 4.6/5 on Capterra across 13 reviews. On G2, a[reviewer at an IT services company](https://www.g2.com/products/manageengine-asset-explorer/reviews/manageengine-asset-explorer-review-12584724) says it’s easy to customize, from adding asset attributes to bulk updates, and that modules like CMDB, purchasing, and remote connection set it apart.


On Capterra, an[IT head at a financial services firm](https://www.capterra.com/p/162097/Site24x7/#Capterra___6787929/) says built-in contract and vendor management, including automated reminders before contracts expire, made procurement and renewals easy. A[reviewer in higher education](https://www.capterra.com/p/162097/Site24x7/#Capterra___6799944/) says tying discovered hardware to employee accounts helped limit losses and speed up troubleshooting, and a[computer operator in the automotive industry](https://www.capterra.com/p/162097/Site24x7/#Capterra___6794464/) found audit prep far easier with hardware and software details already organized.


Plan for some setup and manual work, though: the IT head says entering vendor details and contract terms took a lot of time without bulk import, a[Capterra reviewer who tested agentless scanning](https://www.capterra.com/p/162097/Site24x7/#Capterra___6792231/) saw discrepancies for computers on a different subnet or behind a VPN and had to set up credential sets and discovery rules themselves, and the G2 reviewer notes you may need Active Directory integration to add computers.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Contract and vendor tracking with renewal reminders


No bulk import for vendor and contract data


Ties hardware to employees, limiting losses


Discovery setup is manual across subnets and VPNs


### Pricing


Free edition for up to 25 assets that never expire. Cloud plans start at $115/month or $1,245/year for 250 IT assets, and on-premises licenses start at $955/year for 250 IT assets. A 30-day free trial covers up to 250 assets.


### Key features


-


**Flexible discovery:** Find devices with agent-based or agentless scans and keep inventory records up to date in real time.


-


**Scanner support:** Use barcode, QR code, or RFID scanners to quickly check devices during physical inventory audits.


-


**Purchase and contract management:** Keep purchase orders, vendors, and cost centers together so you can track what you bought and where the money is going.


## 8. ServiceNow ITAM


ServiceNow IT Asset Management runs on the Now Platform alongside ServiceNow's service management tools, which suits large enterprises already on ServiceNow. Its Hardware Asset Management application automates lifecycle tasks like deploy, swap, and retire, and adds stockroom management, contract renewals, shipping carrier integration, and Zebra RFID support.


ServiceNow's IT Asset Management module keeps asset data connected to the rest of your workflows. It’s rated 4.4/5 on G2 across 169 reviews. A[network engineer on G2](https://www.g2.com/products/servicenow-it-asset-management/reviews/servicenow-it-asset-management-review-12540769) highlights its centralized asset tracking and integration with other ServiceNow modules, saying lifecycle automation improves efficiency and reduces manual work.


On TrustRadius, an[OCI architect](https://www.trustradius.com/reviews/servicenow-it-asset-management-2024-12-25-19-42-33) praises its centralized inventory for managing resource assignments and its variety of integration options. However, implementation is the price of admission. The network engineer found the initial setup and configuration complex and time-consuming, and the architect says license costs are high for small companies.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Centralized tracking tied to other ServiceNow modules


Complex, time-consuming initial setup


Wide range of integration options


Expensive licenses for small companies


### Pricing


ServiceNow doesn't publish ITAM pricing. Quotes come through the sales team.


### Key features


-


**Lifecycle automation:** Automate the busywork around sending, swapping, returning, and retiring devices as employees move through the company.


-


**Stockroom and logistics:** Keep tabs on what’s in stock, where it needs to go, and when shipments are on the way with built-in carrier integrations.


-


**Contract management** : Keep contracts tied to the right assets, track renewal dates, and stay ahead of upcoming expirations.


## 9. Electric


Electric is an IT platform for small and midsize businesses, and its Free plan covers hardware visibility at no cost. That plan includes an embedded hardware store, asset tracking, device assignment by employee, and access from inside your payroll platform. Paid tiers add SaaS app management and, on Pro, MDM and automation powered by Electric's Gigawatt AI.


If you’re a small business that wants basic hardware tracking at no cost, Electric’s Free plan is an easy place to start. G2 users rate Electric 4.8/5 across 7 reviews, and Capterra rates it 3.7/5 across 23 reviews. On G2, a[head of people operations](https://www.g2.com/products/electric-ai-electric/reviews/electric-review-12628333) says provisioning a laptop for a new hire used to take one to two hours and now takes about five minutes, and that they use Electric to track each laptop’s health, warranty, lifespan, and security risks.


A[chief of staff](https://www.g2.com/products/electric-ai-electric/reviews/electric-review-11510291) says Electric handles procuring and configuring laptops and setting up accounts and permissions, saving their internal team significant time, and a[VP of operations](https://www.g2.com/products/electric-ai-electric/reviews/electric-review-10823808) values the direct view into their fleet’s status, including automatic emails that walk employees through fixing their own issues.


**Pros**


**Cons**


Laptop provisioning in minutes, not hours


Support can be inconsistent


Clear view of device fleet status


Some early technical hiccups


### Pricing


Free at $0/user/month, which is about as low-risk as IT inventory tracking software gets. Essentials costs $10/user/month, and Pro costs $25/user/month, with volume pricing available.


### Key features


-


**Free asset tracking:** Inventory and device assignment by employee at no cost.


-


**Embedded hardware store:** Order devices from inside the platform.


-


**Payroll platform access:** Hardware visibility inside the payroll tool you already use.


## What is IT inventory management software? Key features and benefits


IT inventory management software keeps one current record of every device and software license a company owns: who has it, where it is, and what condition it's in. It replaces spreadsheets with records that update automatically from discovery scans, HR changes, and device check-ins, giving IT[complete visibility into devices and access](https://www.rippling.com/blog/introducing-it-management-complete-visibility-and-control-over-all-things-it) . Most IT asset inventory management software handles the same core tasks, but tools differ in how much of the physical work they handle. Some only track assets, while others, like Rippling IT and Firstbase, also store, ship, and retrieve devices.


### Key features


-


**Automated discovery:** Scan company devices through agent-based or agentless discovery and automatically add details like device type, operating system, and hardware information to inventory records.


-


**Assignment tracking:** See who has each device, where it's located, when it was assigned, and whether its status has changed. Integrations with HR systems can update assignments as employees join, change roles, or leave.


-


**Software license tracking:** Keep a record of purchased licenses, assigned users, renewal dates, and available seats so IT can spot unused licenses and avoid unnecessary renewals.


-


**Lifecycle management:** Follow each device from purchase and initial deployment through repairs, employee transfers, returns, redeployment, and secure disposal.


-


**Reporting:** Pull reports on inventory counts, device status, condition, location, and ownership to support audits, budgeting, and day-to-day IT decisions.


### Benefits


-


**Fewer devices written off:** Automated retrieval and return tracking mean laptops come back because the system automatically requests them, not because someone happened to remember. This reduces the likelihood of incurring write-offs that you’ll need to replace for the next person.


-


**Lower hardware and software spend:** Reassigning a returned laptop to the next hire always beats incurring the expense of a replacement. And with license tracking, you can surface the seats people haven’t used for ages and cut them out to save money on your subscription spend.


-


**Faster, stronger onboarding experience** : New hires receive configured devices on their first day, rather than a loaner and a vague promise of a fully provisioned device.


-


**Audit readiness:** PwC research cited in Rippling’s[IT Leader's Playbook](https://www.rippling.com/resources/it-leaders-compliance-playbook) found that 47% of organizations failed a formal audit 2–5 times in the past three years, while 18% cite manual evidence collection as their top challenge. A single up-to-date record, plus data-wiping documentation, means that you’re always ready for[IT compliance](https://www.rippling.com/blog/it-compliance) reviews and audits and don’t need to scramble to find the evidence you need.


Effortlessly manage your IT systems

## How to choose the right IT inventory management software


Use these checks to narrow your shortlist. For a formal evaluation, an[IT management software RFP template](https://www.rippling.com/blog/it-management-software-enterprises-rfp-template) turns the evaluation into a set of questions that every vendor answers in writing.


### 1. Decide how much of the logistics you want to own


If you ship and manage a small number of devices per quarter and your ops team already handles it with little hassle or lost time, you may not yet need a full-spectrum IT inventory management platform. At this stage, a tracker like Snipe-IT or AssetExplorer can be a valuable, low-lift addition.


However, once you start shipping across borders or managing a high quantity of hardware, admin overload tends to kick in. Comprehensive platforms like Rippling and Firstbase can help your IT team handle all inventory management tasks (from shipping to retrieval or sale) while reducing manual overhead.


### 2. Confirm offboarding flow


If it’s not immediately clear from your discussions with the vendor or the product documentation they provide you with, ask the following questions to understand how offboarding works in each platform:


-


What triggers retrieval? Does it automatically trigger with an HR status change, or does someone need to file a ticket manually?


-


Who receives the shipping label, the employee or the manager?


-


How are returns tracked?


-


Where are devices physically routed to, and what happens to them when they arrive?


### 3. Map integrations


Prioritize platforms that integrate with your full suite of external tools to minimize additional changes required during implementation. Generally speaking, the more integrations you have, the more capabilities you unlock. For instance:


-


Connecting your **HRIS** lets device orders update in real time when employee changes occur (such as promotions or start-date shifts). Without this link, your IT team is likely rekeying every roster change by hand and learning about them after the fact.


-


Connecting your **service desk** or ticketing tool means that records update automatically as you close tickets, and whoever’s working the queue can see what’s in stock without opening a second system.


With Rippling, inventory runs off the same record as HR and is accessible by default. If you want an all-in-one, connected system to run inventory management, Rippling provides that capability. If you still want to run your workflows through your existing tech stack, Rippling offers a library of 650+ integrations for third-party apps.


Rippling offers a library of 650+ integrations, among the largest in its product category.


### 4. Do the math on your own headcount, not the headline price


Run your own numbers using each platform’s pricing model to get a tangible idea of your total cost. A headline pricing model that looks optimal on the surface may turn out to be wildly more expensive than expected when you take a more detailed look.


Electric bills per user, NinjaOne per device, Freshservice per agent, and AssetExplorer by asset count. Firstbase, Asset Panda, and ServiceNow quote custom pricing. Rippling offers modular pricing, letting you pay only for the modules you actually need.


For example, take a 200-person company with 260 devices and four IT admins.


-


**Per-user pricing** at a rate of $10/user/month lands you at a total of $2,000/month


-


**Per-device pricing** at a rate of $2.50/device/month lands you at $650/month


-


**Per-agent pricing** at a rate of $49/agent/month lands you at $196/month


-


**By-asset-count** pricing at a rate of $1,245/year for 250 assets lands you at $104/month, plus the next tier for the extra 10


-


**Modular pricing** means that you pay only for what you need, nothing more and nothing less


### 5. Run a trial


Rippling, NinjaOne, Freshservice, Asset Panda, and AssetExplorer all offer free trials, and Snipe-IT is free to self-host.


Use your trial window to test the platform’s ability to handle the workflows that are causing you trouble. Observe whether or not (and if so, how) each solution adds value in a live environment. For example, you might:


-


Add a device and assign it to someone, then reassign it to a different employee to see how updates reflect in the inventory system


-


Mark a device as returned and back in stock, then see whether or not you can find it again in your pool of available devices


-


Build a report of every device with key information (who has it, where it is, and what its status is), assessing its accuracy and data quality

## Frequently Asked Questions about IT inventory management


What is the best software for IT inventory management?


It depends on how much of the physical work you want handled. Rippling IT fits teams that want a high degree of automation and a full-spectrum IT module that syncs with all relevant employee data. Firstbase suits organizations that need global logistics handled. Snipe-IT and AssetExplorer are low-cost trackers, while NinjaOne, Freshservice, and ServiceNow are for teams that want assets within endpoint or service management.


What are the top 5 inventory management software options?


Based on this guide, the top five are Rippling IT, Snipe-IT, NinjaOne, Firstbase, and Asset Panda.


What’s the difference between IT inventory management and IT asset management?


IT inventory management tracks what devices and software you have, where they are, and who has them. IT asset management (ITAM) goes further, covering each asset's cost, contracts, licenses, and lifecycle from purchase to disposal. Many tools do both, so the real difference is how much lifecycle and financial detail you need.


How do I choose the right IT inventory management system?


Consider the size of your organization, the types of assets you need to track, the level of automation and integration, and your budget. Assess different solutions based on the feature checklist above. Look for a provider that supports your needs and has a track record with similar companies. Take advantage of free trials to test systems before committing.


Do small businesses need IT inventory management software?


Yes.[Small businesses and startups](https://www.rippling.com/blog/it-management-platform-for-startups) can benefit from IT inventory management software once they have enough devices, employees, or remote workers to make manual tracking difficult. The software creates a central record of company-owned laptops, monitors, phones, and other equipment, making it easier to track assignments, returns, replacements, and inventory as the team grows.


What IT assets can I track with IT inventory software?


You can track any physical hardware, like laptops, desktops, mobile devices, servers, printers, or network equipment. Teams can also monitor software licenses, cloud subscriptions, and peripherals like monitors and keyboards. Some solutions support non-IT assets or include modules specifically for them.


What are the key capabilities of IT inventory management software?


They often include:


-


Cataloging assets with detailed device information


-


Assigning and tracking assets by user, location, and status


-


Managing software licenses and subscriptions


-


Scheduling maintenance, work orders, and asset health checks


-


Managing asset lifecycle events, including reporting, audits, and end-of-life disposal
